items.title: Karnataka’s voter purge mapped: Bengaluru, women, and young voters bear the brunt
items.summary: For every male voter struck off Karnataka’s electoral rolls during the recently concluded Special Intensive Revision (SIR), two female voters were deleted. No clear pattern in voter deletions in relation to seats held by BJP or Congress could be determined from the draft rolls. These are among the major findings of an analysis of the draft rolls of Karnataka’s SIR by the Sabar Institute. The Sabar Institute analysed the SIR’s deletions against the 2023 and 2018 assembly elections results, the Census 2011, and official district income figures, in its recently released preliminary report. The SIR began in Karnataka on June 20 and the final rolls were published on October 27. In the draft electoral rolls published, one in five people, or 20% of the 2023 electorate, were taken off the rolls for various reasons. The final electoral rolls published on October 27 had 4,55,00,011 names against 5,54,32,314 names in the earlier roll, a decrease of 99,32,303 voters.
